events.output:
Sourdough Starters: What Actually Matters (and What Doesn't)

Most new bakers kill their starter with attention, not neglect. A starter needs three things: flour, water and a stable temperature around 24-26 C. Whole-grain rye or whole wheat in the first week speeds things up because it carries more wild yeast and bacteria.

The 'hooch' (grey liquid on top) just means it's hungry. Pour it off or stir it in.

You don't need filtered water unless your tap water is heavily chlorinated; leaving it out overnight is enough.

A starter is ready when it reliably doubles within 4-8 hours of feeding, usually after 7-14 days. The float test is unreliable.

Once established, a starter can live in the fridge and be fed once a week.

Don't name it until week two. Statistically, that's when people give up.

random q from Leo at breakfast: why do leaves change colour in the fall?

Because the green was hiding the other colours all along.
- Leaves are green from chlorophyll, which the tree uses to make food from sunlight
- When days get shorter and cooler, the tree stops making chlorophyll and the green fades
- The yellows and oranges (carotenoids) were there all summer, just covered up
- Reds and purples (anthocyanins) are made fresh in fall, especially after sunny days and cool nights, which is why maples go so red
- Then the tree seals off the leaf and it drops
Kid version: the leaf takes off its green coat and shows the colours underneath.

Chickpea and spinach coconut curry, about 30 minutes.
- Start rice first (1 cup rice, 1.5 cups water, 15 min covered, 5 min rest)
- Soften 1 onion, 3 garlic cloves and a thumb of ginger in oil, 5 min
- Add 1 tbsp curry powder, 1 tsp cumin, half tsp turmeric, stir 1 min
- Add 1 can drained chickpeas, 1 can coconut milk, half a can of diced tomatoes if you have them; simmer 10 min
- Stir in 4 big handfuls of spinach until wilted, finish with lime juice and salt
